rows.rationale: Preserves disturbing divine agency, second-person possible subject and conditional offering clause.
rows.before: Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When you make his life an offering for guilt, he will see offspring; he will prolong his days; the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
rows.after: Yet the **LORD** desired to crush him and make him sick. If you make his life a reparation offering, he will see offspring and prolong his days, and the **LORD**’s purpose will prosper in his hand.
rows.tsw_comparator: Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When you make his life an offering for guilt, he shall see offspring; he shall prolong his days; the will of the LORD shall prosper in his hand.

rows.rationale: Preserves terse paired acts; equivalence versus combined practices noted.
rows.before: The one who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; the one who sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; the one who presents a grain offering, like one who presents pig’s blood; the one who makes a memorial offering of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.
rows.after: One slaughters an ox—and kills a person; one sacrifices a lamb—and breaks a dog’s neck; one brings a grain offering—and pig’s blood; one burns memorial incense—and blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways and delight in their offensive things.
rows.tsw_comparator: The one who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; the one who sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; the one who presents a grain offering, like one who presents pig’s blood; the one who makes a memorial offering of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.
